findings.desc: Canonicalization advertises and persists glob rules, but pathMatchesScopePattern is not a glob matcher. Patterns such as packages/main/src/**/*.ts, src/foo?.ts, character classes, and brace patterns are detected as rule='glob' by pathRule yet only exact/subtree, a trailing-star strip, or basename '*.ext' are matched. This can fail open for protectedFiles/explicitExcludes globs and fail closed spuriously for allowed globs, violating the required preservation of exact/glob semantics. Implement one bounded canonical glob grammar shared by all consumers and add positive/negative protected and allowed glob regressions.

The whole-artifact gap binding can launder pre-existing tampering. appendGapFinding reads the current findings array, never verifies its existing binding/signatures, appends a new finding, then signs a digest that includes every earlier record. Thus a direct edit to an older finding followed by any legitimate non-dedup gap_log call produces a new valid latest binding over the altered history; verifyGapLogArtifactBinding verifies only the latest finding signature and will trust the artifact. Require a valid current official binding before extending a bound artifact (with an explicit legacy migration path), and/or verify the complete signed chain rather than only the latest record. Add regression: valid artifact -> mutate old finding -> gap_log new distinct gap -> classifier must remain fail-closed.

The policy truth sources were not synchronized with the shipped shared-metadata gate. lifecycle-artifact-scope.md still states there are only three classifier outputs and does not specify the exact B-META path, official gap_log whole-artifact binding, fail-closed mismatch/forgery/copy/symlink behavior, or that scope and done_prepare share this classifier. workflow-convergence-failure-remediation-execution-plan.md also lacks the shipped repo-relative-v1 / TypeScript AST version and independent rollout contract. Update those two canonical decision docs minimally so operational policy matches the new L4 process fact and code.

AST declaration binding uses the full unified hunk range, not the changed-line span. buildScopeDiffPack always requests --unified=20, while parserBackedAnchor only accepts a declaration when node.getFullStart() <= hunk start AND node.end >= hunk end. A short function surrounded by 20 context lines therefore degrades to file scope; file_scope_no_enclosing_declaration is not treated as parser failure, so protectedAnchors can silently miss the touched function. The focused test constructs @@ ...,1 hunks and does not exercise the production --unified=20 range. Compute anchors from actual +/- changed line positions (or a set of changed spans) and fail closed when a protected semantic contract cannot bind them; add a production-shaped regression.

AST protected-anchor enforcement can be bypassed when one unified diff hunk spans more than one declaration. parserBackedAnchor requires one declaration node to enclose the entire hunk range (scope-diff-pack.ts:135-139), but the range includes up to 20 context lines and can span adjacent declarations. It then emits file_scope_no_enclosing_declaration; semantic-scope-gate.ts does not treat that fallback as fail-closed (only parse_error/source_unavailable at lines 140-143), so protectedAnchors are not observed and the gate returns PASS. Repro against 01590a312a: parseUnifiedDiff for scope-path-classifier.ts hunk @@ -69,120 +69,120 @@ yielded current+previous file anchors; checkSemanticScope with protectedAnchors=[canonicalizeScopePath] returned status=pass, violations=[]. Split/attribute changed line ranges to every touched declaration, or make multi-declaration/file fallback fail closed whenever semantic protections exist.
